texts: mixed: faithful and fireable, but the two phases are locked inside an opaque 'or' that the reasoner never opens, so 'when do spring tides occur?' returns nothing and 'is this spring tide at new moon?' stays unknown. If you need the phases queryable, split them into two sentences — "Spring tides occur at new moon." and "Spring tides occur at full moon." — and do not join them with 'and' in one sentence, which would claim each tide happens at both.

bad: three problems, all traceable to the phrasing. 'Time X to Y' has no representation, so the alignment came out as a spatial destination, as if the harvest were being moved to the tide; 'the new-moon spring tide' entered the knowledge base as a bare label with no type and no link to 'tide'; and 'the Keepers' is ambiguous between a name and a plural group, so a per-member rule was generated that the sentence does not license. Put the timing directly on the harvest and let the tide be an ordinary thing: "Keepers harvest salt-bloom during the spring tide that occurs at the new moon." — that keeps who, what and when, and makes the time answerable, at the cost of the explicit 'they schedule it for' nuance.
